newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds decline on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds decline on profit taking.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed slightly lower on Tuesday as investors took profits after a strong rally on Monday, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.02 pct to 105.13
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.03 pct to 105.24
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 105.08
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.38 to 104.34
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 to 103.92
Volume was a low 133 million shekels.
"The market is stabilising after it rose sharply. We saw some profit taking in CPI-linked bonds," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House. CPI-linked bonds had surged 0.26 percent on Monday.

"These bonds made an enormous move with yields on long bonds falling from 5.3 percent in August to only 4.07 to 4.1 percent. The main question is if the market is strong enough to push yields below four percent," Weisberg added.

Traders noted inflation-linked bonds were also affected by the fact that the Treasury is to offer 200 million shekels worth of bonds this week and another 200 million shekels worth next week. It usually issues bonds for 100 million shekels a week.

"The fact that inflation-linked bonds remained stable after Monday's sharp rise shows the market's strength. The rise of long CPI-linked bonds is a clear indication that the market awaits another rate cut," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblgon Securities.

Israel Discount Bank said in a report released on Tuesday that interest rates will fall by 0.5 percentage point during the second quarter due to a slowing economy but will hold steady in the third quarter.
"Unlinked bonds continued their slow rise. Investors expect that the slowing economy will also lead to lower inflation," Eidelheit added.
"All the indicators show a slowdown in economic activity. There is more talk now of the possibility of a new economic plan which will include a rate cut," Weisberg said.

The Israeli financial daily Globes reported on Monday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will convene a meeting on Sunday with Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel on the budget deficit and growth.
Dollar-linked bonds continued to rise as the shekel declined against the dollar. In local trading the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3890 shekels against 3.3810 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.39 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
